items.q: In the bilateral pathogenesis drawing, both arteries carry a red cross and the legend beside it reads 'x – Occlusion'.
opts: True — the crosses stand for occlusion on either side
False — the crosses mark the clip used in the unilateral model
False — only one artery is crossed in the bilateral drawing
True — and the same legend defines 'x' as a stenosis of less than 80%
items.exp: The unilateral drawing shows a clip on one limb, whereas the bilateral drawing crosses both limbs and prints the red legend 'x – Occlusion', explaining why neither kidney can escape the low perfusion. (Book p751)

items.q: The flowchart attributes recurrent flash pulmonary edema in bilateral renal artery stenosis to:
opts: Intravascular edema, written in brackets after the phrase
Low oncotic pressure from nephrotic syndrome
items.exp: Printed line: 'Recurrent flash pulmonary edema (D/t intravascular edema)', reached from ↑Na+/H2O retention and intravascular volume overload, and treated with B/L PTRA with stenting. (Book p751)

items.q: Besides blood-pressure control, which pair of general measures appears under treatment of bilateral renal artery stenosis?
opts: Start ACE inhibitors and restrict protein
Begin dual antiplatelet therapy and anticoagulate
items.exp: The treatment block lists In BP → diuretics (DOC) and ACE inhibitors/ARBs contraindicated as they ↓GFR, followed by 'Stop smoking' and 'Start statins'. (Book p751)

items.q: A smoker with bilateral RAS and an ejection fraction of 60% returns with two episodes of overnight breathlessness; CDU confirms bilateral stenosis. The page's sequence predicts the episodes are due to:
opts: Intravascular volume overload from loss of pressure natriuresis, managed by B/L PTRA with stenting
Rise in RIHP driving natriuresis, managed by an ACE inhibitor
Arteriopathy of fibromuscular dysplasia, managed by PTRA alone
Medullary hypoxia, managed by statins and smoking cessation
items.exp: Bilateral occlusion removes the pressure-natriuresis escape (↓RIHP → ↑Na+/H2O retention → volume overload → recurrent flash pulmonary edema), for which the flowchart's Rx is B/L percutaneous transluminal renal angioplasty with stenting; statins and stopping smoking are the additional measures. (Book p751)
